final_message:
I couldn't reproduce the bug, so I haven't changed anything.

`median` in `src/stats_utils.py` already averages the two middle values for even-length lists. I ran `median([1, 2, 3, 4])` and it returned `2.5`. `tests/test_stats_utils.py` also has an even-length case (`median([4, 1, 3, 2]) == 2.5`), and this is the only `median` in the repo.

The users may be running a different version than this checkout, such as an older release or an installed copy of the package. They may also be using a different function, or passing something other than a plain list (for example, a custom type whose sorting or division behaves differently).

If you can tell me which version the users have, or give me an example of how they call it, I'll look into it. If you have a branch or commit where it does return `3`, point me to it and I'll check there.
